entities.summary: Inscriptiones Latinae Selectae, standard abbreviation ILS, is a three-volume selection of Latin inscriptions edited by Hermann Dessau. The work was published in five parts serially from 1892 to 1916, with numerous reprints. Supporting material and notes are all written in Latin. Inscriptions are organized within chapters (capita, singular caput) by topic, such as funerary inscriptions, or inscriptions pertaining to collegia. Each inscription has an identifying number. Scholars citing a Latin inscription will often provide the ILS number in addition to a reference for the more comprehensive Corpus Inscriptionum Latinarum (CIL); for example, CIL 12.2.774—ILS 39.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: ILS is a foundational work in the study of Latin inscriptions, providing critical cataloging and analysis that has informed scholarship for centuries. Its comprehensive coverage of inscriptions from across the Roman world has enabled scholars to reconstruct historical events and cultural practices with greater precision.
